scope.selection_constraint: Latest user instruction restricts selection to the current61-class context; no outside candidates were added in this integration pass.

findings.title: Isolated verifier omitted new dependencies
findings.before: Hardcoded old core order and Quantum/Normalization/Complete omitted the new imported modules, preventing a fresh trusted sandbox build.
findings.fix: Derive deterministic dependency order from hash-checked trusted first-party source headers. Validate paths, source/hash-set equality, missing imports and cycles. Keep candidate imports out of discovery and keep explicit checker/baseline stages.
findings.validation: Actual shipped graph includes all33 first-party modules; missing root/dependency, cycles, invalid paths and hashes fail closed. Final remote replay belongs to parent integration checks.

findings.title: External inclusion census indexed background complements through a scored-only map
findings.before: Mapping only scored IDs made retained background complement identities raise KeyError.
findings.fix: Build discovery mapping from context_ids; report scope retains context paths.
findings.validation: Tiny local HTML inclusion graph processes all61 IDs and confirms P subset NP without a network request.

findings.title: Proof review ignored trusted semantic/checker/baseline report identities
findings.before: A maintainer-supplied report with matching dataset, claims and proof-source hash could carry stale or incorrect semantics_sha256, checker_sha256 and baseline_sha256.
findings.fix: Generation and admission now share trusted_verification_inputs. Admission requires the actual method and all three exact current bindings, including the report's full ordered target list. Missing legacy identities are rejected.
findings.validation: All three mismatches and omissions reject; changing a real semantic file or checker support file rejects an otherwise matching report; exactly matching report passes.
findings.boundary: This prevents accidental stale report reuse. Reports and review registries remain explicit trusted maintainer inputs; no cryptographic signature authenticates arbitrary JSON supplied by a malicious maintainer.

findings.title: Root Lean imports absent from frozen formalization manifest
findings.before: Changing either shipped root entry point did not change or invalidate the formalization bundle.
findings.validation: Mutating either root in a temporary frozen fixture now makes frozen_release reject; restoring both passes.

findings.title: Published model evidence URL always selected main
findings.before: The public row could link branch-specific published evidence to main.
findings.validation: Read the updated construction; no real model evaluation was fabricated or published.

findings.title: Descriptive JSONSchemas rejected every new endpoint
findings.before: All six endpoint enums retained the old50 identifiers, even though runtime and provider schema accepted the full61 context.
findings.fix: generate_schemas.py refreshes endpoint enums from all catalog classes during import/release generation. Reproducibility checking includes the three files.
findings.validation: Equality tests compare every left/right enum with context_ids, retain background coRP and accept QMA2/ExistsR; future-node fixture verifies generation is not hardcoded to61.

risk_assessment.judgment: No unresolved blocking defect found in the exercised integration boundaries after these fixes. This is a bounded code/fixture review, not a calibrated probability of zero bugs.
risk_assessment.high_fanout_paths_examined: A background scoring leak, a truncated inference vocabulary, or a stale semantic report could affect many pairs; tests exercise these paths explicitly rather than inferring safety from the matrix dimensions.
residual_risks: The trusted literature/model-equivalence boundary and quality of historical review remain external to these software checks.
Maintainers can fabricate or manually edit trusted registries; this design does not defend against a malicious maintainer.
Future trusted Lean header syntax outside the documented restricted parser fails closed and needs a corresponding parser/test update.
Actual Docker/Lean execution of the new topological order remains a required release integration check.
No whole-application browser replay was repeated here; source inspection and generated graph tests cover the data/UI boundary.
